cardinal_symptoms: Inflammatory lesions (papules, pustules, nodules, and cysts)
urgent_escalation_criteria: Acne fulminans (requires same-day urgent referral to on-call hospital dermatology team to be assessed within 24 hours)
Significant psychological distress, suicidal ideation, or self-harm
Presence of nodulocystic acne failing two different 3-6 month oral antibiotic courses

differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_features: Presence of menstrual irregularities alongside acne
Current use of oral steroids, anabolic steroids, progesterone-only contraception, or certain anticonvulsants

investigations.rationale: Acne vulgaris is diagnosed clinically. Routine microbiological and endocrinological investigations are not recommended unless ruling out underlying mimicking conditions.

acute_management_sequence.details: Advise the patient to use a non-alkaline (skin pH neutral or slightly acidic) synthetic detergent cleansing product twice daily. Make-up, moisturisers, and sunscreens must be non oil-based and non-comedogenic. Inform patients that picking lesions increases scarring risk.

Offer a 12-week course of topical treatment. To reduce initial skin irritation, advise starting with alternate-day or short-contact application (washing off after one hour), progressing to standard application as tolerated. Positive effects take 6-8 weeks.

specific_drugs.drug_name: Adapalene with Benzoyl peroxide fixed combination
Benzoyl peroxide with Clindamycin fixed combination

acute_management_sequence.details: Offer a 12-week course combining a fixed topical treatment (such as Adapalene with Benzoyl peroxide or topical Azelaic acid) with a systemic oral antibiotic. Oral and topical antibiotics should NOT be used in combination to prevent resistance.
Following completion of oral antibiotics, consider fixed combination topical adapalene and benzoyl peroxide as maintenance treatment to reduce the risk of relapse.

disposition_criteria.follow_up_timeline: Review at 12 weeks to assess clinical response and adverse effects.
